key_insight: Physics-informed PDE solvers can improve accuracy not only by updating weights, but by dynamically reshaping model capacity where the residual physics is hardest to resolve.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical adaptive-computation strategy for stiff, heterogeneous 3D/4D PDEs, concentrating parameters where they matter and pruning them where they do not.
method: Representation Capacity Adaptation for PDEs (ReCAP) uses Gaussian-localized components to redistribute capacity during training.
It refines the model with residual-directed splitting, gate-based pruning, and function-aware merging.
Quiet-child refinement initializes new components by transporting the parent representation to reduce disruption from splitting.
evidence_signal: Across five challenging 3D and 4D PDE benchmarks against 11 physics-informed solvers, ReCAP achieved the lowest relative L2 error on every problem, with 10.7%–27.5% improvement over the strongest competitor.
watch_item: Dynamic splitting/merging adds algorithmic complexity and may require careful tuning of residual indicators and stability controls to avoid unstable or overly frequent restructuring.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Neural Plasticity: PDE Solvers That Reshape Themselves
